before: The public class Labels belongs to package study, so its qualified name is study.Labels. Keep its source at study/Labels.java. An import lets Main use the shorter name; it does not download or copy code.
Expected output or behavior: review. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add a second public helper in the same package and list both sources in the compile command. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A package groups named classes. Labels belongs to study, so its full name is study.Labels. Put its source in study/Labels.java. The import lets Main use the short name Labels; it does not download or copy the class.

The class path tells Java where to start looking for compiled classes. In a practice folder, compile with javac --release 25 -d classes Main.java study/Labels.java, then run java -cp classes Main. classes is the search root above the study folder.
The program prints review. Main finds the imported Labels class and calls its public static name method.
The quiz changes only the imported package name. Check whether the available source declares a class under that name.

before.question: What happens if the import says missing.Labels instead?
choices: Java downloads it from a package registry.
Compilation fails because that imported type is unavailable.
before.explanation: Import resolves a qualified type name against available sources or classes; no dependency is fetched.

after.question: Change the import to missing.Labels. What happens?
choices: Compilation fails because that imported class is unavailable.
after.explanation: The available class is study.Labels, not missing.Labels. An import uses an existing name; it does not fetch or rename code.
